# Payment Method Events

A connected clause that announces payment instructions and turns payment requests into MyOS execution requests. Both actions emit `Payment Event` envelopes.

- **`announce`** runs automatically on `initialized`, meaning successful initial clause installation. Its automatic connection has `once: true`. It copies `/paymentDetails` into `details` and sets `kind` to `Customer Payment Session Requested` when `/paymentDetails/method` equals `myos-customer`; otherwise it uses `Account Payment Instruction Created`.
- **`request`** runs automatically for an `Event` matching `kind: Payment Requested`. It emits `kind: MyOS Execution Requested`, with `details` copied from `/paymentDetails`, `method` copied from `/paymentDetails/method`, and `request` containing the triggering event. This automatic connection is not once-only; subsequent matching events can produce further requests.

The paths refer to the document where this clause executes, including a nested instruction’s own document. Values are read when each action runs. The type supplies no payment-detail schema, required method value, or method default. Missing details remain unknown; the announcement’s alternative label does not establish a default payment method.

Inherited connection configuration allows additional named connections under `bindings.announce` and `bindings.request`; `_automatic` is reserved. A connection’s `when` can skip execution, while `parameters.conditions.announce` or `parameters.conditions.request` can reject execution with `ACTION_CONDITION_FAILED`. These conditions default to true when omitted. Connections may add `before` and `after` behavior and set Boolean `once`, which defaults to false. A once-only connection records that it fired after its action and follow-up behavior; this records connection execution, not payment success. Changing an installed clause’s configuration requires a new clause key.

The declared action bodies append events without payment-specific validation or payment-status updates. Their emissions do not confirm that a customer session exists, MyOS executed the request, or funds moved. Event authority comes from authenticated input or document origin, not from the event’s name.
